summary: Oregon L-4 cab on a timber tower in the Bull of the Woods Wilderness, built in 1942 and lost to the Bull Complex Fire in September 2021.

facts.design: L-4 cab on a timber tower (register); tower height disputed
facts.status_note: Lost to fire activity in the Bull Complex Fire, September 2021. No source we read describes what, if anything, remains.

access.note: Inside the Bull of the Woods Wilderness and reached on foot. We did not find a current access notice.

visit.trail_note: A 3.2-mile hike in, per a 2005 item. The lookout was lost in 2021, so there is no cab to climb.

events.note: First cabin on the site, a log cabin with a cupola. KTVZ and the Forest Lookouts timeline give 1928; firelookout.com gives 1923; the register says the 1920s.
Staffed for 74 days, per the Forest Lookouts timeline.
Current L-4 cab built on a timber tower; the register says the tower frame was prefabricated at a CCC camp.
Last staffed 1963 or 1964 per the register; KTVZ says staffed each year until 1964, then intermittently by volunteers until the 1980s.
Deactivated as a lookout, per the Forest Lookouts timeline.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register on December 30, 1996.

A 2005 PIT Traveler item quoted on the Forest Lookouts page says volunteers and Forest Service heritage staff would complete interior and exterior restoration. Completion is not confirmed in our sources.
Bull Complex Fire moved toward the lookout over several weeks.
Lost to fire activity on Sunday, per KTVZ. The Forest Service release dated September 6, 2021 says it was lost the day before.

corrections.why: The register and the 2005 item say the cab sat on a 10-foot tower (about 3.05 m). The current 4.6 m matches the 15-foot tower in the Forest Lookouts timeline, the only source that gives 15 feet. Human review needed.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register, KTVZ and the Forest Service release all say the lookout was lost to the Bull Complex Fire in September 2021, so the gone status stands.

notes_for_editor: Open conflicts: (1) first cabin date: 1920s (register), 1923 (firelookout.com), 1928 (Forest Lookouts timeline and KTVZ). (2) Tower height: 10 ft (register and 2005 item; firelookout.com also gives 10') vs 15 ft (Forest Lookouts timeline). Correction proposed to height_m, human review needed. (3) Elevation: register 5,438 ft (1,658 m), matching the record's 1657.5 m; firelookout.com and the Forest Lookouts page give 5523 ft. (4) Use after 1964: register says occasional backcountry guard station; firelookout.com says only for emergencies; KTVZ says volunteers intermittently to the 1980s. (5) firelookout.com puts it in Marion County; the register and the record say Clackamas, and the record is kept. The loss date 'Sunday' is from KTVZ and the Forest Service release dated 6 Sept 2021 ('yesterday'); no separate primary date was read. Not read: the Oregonian and Statesman Journal articles (both returned 403 or were not fetched), and the Forest Service Facebook post directly; the Facebook quote is read through the cherylhill.net reprint. The register's claim that the structure is listed on the NRHP has no listing date in our sources. The Forest Service reported the lookout lost; no source describes the site after the fire.
